page: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable instance powered by the custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor based on the Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, operating without hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local NVMe storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals that the t4g.xlarge delivers moderate compute performance. In stress-ng testing, it achieves a single-core CPU score of 1519.58 and a multi-core score of 6011.97, both falling within the average range. However, memory and specialized workloads show limitations. The Geekbench single-core score of 885.0 and multi-core score of 3046.0 are categorized as poor and weak respectively. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average at 66.09 GB/sec for reads and 32.48 GB/sec for writes, but small block cached reads are weak at 233.41 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks also register lower-tier results, with a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 20.29 GB/sec and a poor Passmark CPU encryption score of 541.1.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t4g.xlarge offers a budget-friendly entry point for ARM64 development and testing due to its burstable CPU allocation model. This model allows users to pay a lower baseline rate while accumulating credits for temporary spikes in CPU utilization. Given the weak to poor performance in intensive tasks like LLM inference and bzip3 decompression, this instance is not suited for sustained high-compute workloads. It is best utilized for low-traffic web serving, microservices, code repositories, and lightweight database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance operates with 4 physical cores and no hyperthreading. It lacks local storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results position the t4g.xlarge in the average tier for standard compute tasks, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6011.97, but it exhibits weak to poor performance in memory-intensive and cryptographic operations. The burstable CPU allocation model makes this instance a cost-effective option for workloads with variable resource demands. It is best suited for lightweight applications, development environments, and low-traffic web servers.
